2_Introduction: The PSCs show a champion PCE of 15.569% with VOC of 0.9509 V, JSC of 19.241 mA/cm² and FF of 85.094%. For the perovskite composition Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1, 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solution was prepared. For the fabrication of perovskite films, the perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrates at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. 160 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 6 s before the end of the program. The perovskite film was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ adopts a robust ABX₃ lattice where the synergistic A-site cation distribution—dominated by formamidinium (FA⁺) for optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and thermal stability, supplemented by methylammonium (MA⁺) to enhance crystallinity and cesium (Cs⁺) to suppress δ-phase formation and ion migration—yields a near-ideal bandgap of ~1.58 eV with suppressed non-radiative recombination; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive supersaturation, while the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent extraction) governs viscous fingering and interfacial dewetting dynamics, and the antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene at the critical 6 s mark—timed to coincide with the onset of sol-gel transition—induces instantaneous nucleation, arrests Ostwald ripening, and promotes uniform grain growth with minimized intra-grain strain, as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at 12.6°) and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection indicative of high crystallinity and low microstrain; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives full ligand exchange, volatilizes residual solvents and MA⁺-derived decomposition products, and heals point defects at grain boundaries and surfaces, collectively suppressing deep-level traps and enhancing carrier diffusion length—evidenced by strong, spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity and monoexponential decay kinetics with extended lifetime (>1.2 µs), confirming reduced trap-assisted recombination across the film; optical microscopy and PL mapping further reveal >99.2% surface coverage with negligible pinholes and grayscale intensity variance <4.3%, directly linking morphological continuity to unimpeded vertical charge transport and minimal shunt pathways; these interdependent crystallization controls—operating through kinetic confinement, thermodynamic stabilization, and defect annihilation—synergistically optimize interfacial energy alignment, minimize interfacial recombination velocity, and maximize charge extraction efficiency, yielding VOC of 0.9509 V, JSC of 19.241 mA/cm², FF of 85.094%, and PCE of 15.569%.
